Apple___Apple_scab.description: Fungal disease causing dark spots on leaves and deformed fruits.
Apple___Apple_scab.cause: Fungus spread by wind during wet weather.

fertilizers.name: Potassium Sulfate (SOP)
fertilizers.purpose: Apply 400–500 g per tree in early spring; strengthens cell walls, firms the fruit and improves natural disease resistance.

fertilizers.name: Calcium Nitrate
fertilizers.purpose: Spray 5 g per litre of water at fruit-set and again after 15 days; toughens the fruit skin and stops cracking and bitter pit.

fertilizers.name: Farmyard Manure (Compost)
fertilizers.purpose: Mix 20–25 kg per tree in the basin before flowering; feeds the soil and keeps roots healthy all season.

organic_remedy: Collect and burn all fallen infected leaves outside the farm so the fungus cannot survive winter.
Spray Neem oil (5 ml per litre of water) mixed with a pinch of soap every 7 days.
Spray a diluted cow-milk solution (1 part milk to 9 parts water) on a sunny morning to slow the fungus.
chemical_spray: Captan 50% WP (Wettable Powder) — 2.0g per liter. Foliar spray at petal fall, repeat every 7-10 days.
Mancozeb 75% WP (Wettable Powder) — 2.5g per liter. Foliar spray, repeat every 10-14 days.
Myclobutanil 10% WP (Wettable Powder) — 1.0g per liter. Foliar spray during early infection, repeat every 14 days.
Apple___Apple_scab.best_time_to_spray: Early morning (6:00–9:00 AM) or evening after 4:00 PM, when sunlight is mild and there is little wind.
safety_tips: Check the underside of the leaves (patti ke neeche) once a week — spots and insects are easy to stop when small.
Prune the tree so the centre stays open; sunlight and airflow keep the canopy dry and fungus-free.
Collect and burn fallen leaves and fruit in autumn so disease cannot survive the winter.
While spraying any chemical, wear a mask, gloves and full-sleeve clothes, and never spray against the wind.
Keep children and animals away from sprayed plants, and do not harvest before the waiting period printed on the product label.
